config.title: HOC withAuth

intro.title: HOC withAuth
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Higher-Order Component (HOC) called `withAuth` that adds authentication logic to other React components. You will learn how HOCs wrap components to provide reusable functionality, such as checking if a user is logged in before rendering. The main technologies involved are React components, JavaScript functions, and conditional rendering. By the end, you'll understand how to create and apply HOCs to protect parts of your app based on authentication state.
intro.usecase: Higher-Order Components like withAuth are essential for protecting routes and components in real-world applications. You'll see this pattern in dashboard systems where certain admin panels should only be visible to authenticated users with specific permissions. E-commerce platforms use HOCs to guard checkout pages and user profiles, while banking apps apply them to secure transaction histories and account settings. This approach allows developers to reuse authentication logic across multiple components without duplicating code.

objectives: Construct a higher-order component that wraps authentication logic around other components
Initialize and manage authentication state within a HOC
Apply conditional rendering based on authentication status
Configure prop forwarding to maintain component functionality
Integrate the withAuth HOC with existing React components
Manipulate component behavior through authentication checks
Render appropriate UI elements for authenticated and unauthenticated states

steps.title: Create the withAuth higher-order component
steps.instruction: Create a function named withAuth that takes a component as an argument and returns a new component.
steps.hint: A higher-order component is a function that accepts a component and returns a new component. Start by defining a function withAuth that takes a single parameter (the component to wrap).
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a withAuth function defined that follows the HOC pattern: it accepts a component and returns a new component.
successCriteria: A function named withAuth is defined, it takes a component parameter, and it returns a function (or component).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your withAuth function takes a component as a parameter and returns a new function or component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The withAuth function should be defined to accept a component and return a new component. Review the HOC pattern and try again.

steps.title: Add authentication logic to the HOC
steps.instruction: Inside the withAuth function, check if isAuthenticated is true and conditionally return either the wrapped component or a login message.
steps.hint: Use a conditional (if statement or ternary) to check isAuthenticated. If true, return the WrappedComponent with its props. If false, return a simple message like 'Please log in to view this content.'
steps.expectedOutcome: The withAuth function now contains conditional logic that returns the wrapped component when authenticated, or a login message when not.
successCriteria: withAuth function contains a conditional check for isAuthenticated
Returns WrappedComponent with props when authenticated
Returns a login message or element when not authenticated
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking isAuthenticated and returning the appropriate content for both authenticated and unauthenticated states.
steps.feedbackWrong: The withAuth function doesn't yet contain the authentication logic. Add a conditional that checks isAuthenticated and returns either the wrapped component or a login message.

steps.title: Wrap the Profile component with withAuth
steps.instruction: Create an enhanced version of the Profile component by calling withAuth(Profile). Store the result in a variable named AuthenticatedProfile.
steps.hint: Call the withAuth function you created earlier, passing Profile as the argument. Assign the returned enhanced component to a new variable.
